findings.title: Local cache poisoning lets any new device bypass the device limit on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go checks localCache, then calls localCache.SetDefault(key) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the DB returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the cache entry is already stored and never removed. The next request for the same deviceID hits the cache early-return nil, so TagDevice succeeds and Anonymous.Authenticate succeeds. Any blocked device can therefore get anonymous access by making a second request, and transient DB errors also cause permanent 29-minute under-counting. Fix by caching only after successful DB write or evicting on failure.

findings.title: Count-then-insert race allows exceeding the device limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go does CountDevices, then if count < deviceLimit falls through to INSERT. There is no transaction, row lock, or unique count constraint. Two concurrent new devices when count == limit-1 can both observe count < limit and both INSERT different device_ids, ending with limit+1 active devices. Under load, when the limit matters most, it is unenforceable. Fix with atomic guard e.g. serializable transaction, conditional insert, or DB-side enforcement.

findings.title: Anonymous tagging moved from background to synchronous auth hot path
findings.body: Anonymous.Authenticate in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go previously tagged devices in a go routine with context.Background and 2-minute timeout and never blocked login. This PR calls anonDeviceService.TagDevice synchronously with the request ctx, which on cache miss does CountDevices plus INSERT/UPDATE. Every new anonymous login now pays extra DB round-trips and inherits DB slowness/failure, coupling login availability and p99 latency to the anon_device table. Fix by keeping tagging async/off-request or using detached context with timeout for the non-limit path.

findings.title: Provider signature change breaks DI wiring and testability
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go changed from taking anonstore.AnonStore to taking db.DB and constructing ProvideAnonDBStore internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. No wire_gen update is in the PR, so existing generated code passing an AnonStore will fail to compile. It also hard-codes the DB implementation, preventing mocks/fakes or alternate stores. Fix by regenerating wire, or keep injecting AnonStore and inject the limit separately.

findings.title: Unlimited limit sent as 0 mismatches frontend undefined contract
findings.body: FrontendSettingsDTO in pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go adds AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 with json:"anonymousDeviceLimit" and no omitempty, so unlimited (0 in Cfg) serializes as 0. Frontend types declare anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined with default undefined. After lodash merge, 0 overwrites undefined, so UI cannot distinguish unlimited from a zero-device limit if it checks for undefined. Use pointer with omitempty or document that 0 means unlimited on both sides.

findings.title: No test that existing devices can still update when at limit
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go only verifies a second distinct deviceID gets ErrDeviceLimitReached. It never verifies the intended allow-path that an already-counted deviceID can still be updated when count >= limit, nor expiry-window or cache interaction. A regression breaking legitimate returning devices would not be caught. Add a test that re-tags the first device after the limit is reached and expects success and updated timestamp.
